D. All points have a vibration period the same as the vibration plate's period. — TRUE. The period equals the source period.

A. In order to increase the internal energy of a body, work must be done on it or heat must be transferred to it.

B. Doing work on a body must increase its internal energy.
- Not necessarily. If the body does work on surroundings while... wait, "doing work on a body" means W on the body is positive. But the body could simultaneously lose heat, so internal energy could decrease or stay the same. So B is incorrect.

- This violates the second law of thermodynamics (Kelvin statement): it's impossible to construct a heat engine that absorbs heat from a single reservoir and converts it entirely to work. So C is incorrect.

- This is the Kelvin statement of the second law. So D is correct. - Yes, work can be completely converted to heat, but heat cannot be completely converted back to work without other effects; this is an irreversible process. E is correct.
